[2023 fall ms applied — problem 4]

Three fertilizers $\times$ three seed types, 45 plots (5 replicates per combination). ANOVA SS: Seed 16.962, Fertilizer 11.820, Seed:Fertilizer 47.949, Residuals 45.210. (1) Give the degrees of freedom. (2) Test that the fertilizer effect is the same regardless of seed type (no interaction). (3) Test that fertilizer has no effect, for every seed type.

response.text:
Let seed type have \(a=3\) levels, fertilizer have \(b=3\) levels, and replicates per cell be \(r=5\). Thus

\[
N=abr=3\cdot 3\cdot 5=45.
\]

Use the fixed-effects two-way ANOVA model

\[
Y_{ijk}=\mu+\alpha_i+\beta_j+(\alpha\beta)_{ij}+\varepsilon_{ijk},
\qquad \varepsilon_{ijk}\stackrel{iid}{\sim}N(0,\sigma^2).
\]

## (1) Degrees of freedom

\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c|c}
\text{Source} & SS & df & MS\\
\hline
\text{Seed} & 16.962 & 3-1=2 & 8.481\\
\text{Fertilizer} & 11.820 & 3-1=2 & 5.910\\
\text{Seed:Fertilizer} & 47.949 & (3-1)(3-1)=4 & 11.987\\
\text{Residual} & 45.210 & 3\cdot 3(5-1)=36 & 1.2558\\
\hline
\text{Total} & 121.941 & 45-1=44 &
\end{array}
\]

So the degrees of freedom are:

\[
2,\ 2,\ 4,\ 36,\ 44.
\]

---

## (2) Test no interaction

The hypothesis “the fertilizer effect is the same regardless of seed type” is the no-interaction hypothesis:

\[
H_0 : (\alpha\beta)_{ij}=0 \ \text{for all } i,j.
\]

The test statistic is

\[
F=\frac{MS_{\text{Seed:Fertilizer}}}{MS_E}
=\frac{47.949/4}{45.210/36}.
\]

Compute:

\[
MS_{\text{int}}=\frac{47.949}{4}=11.98725,
\qquad
MS_E=\frac{45.210}{36}=1.25583.
\]

Thus

\[
F=\frac{11.98725}{1.25583}=9.545.
\]

Under \(H_0\),

\[
F\sim F_{4,36}.
\]

The \(p\)-value is approximately

\[
p \approx 2.3\times 10^{-5}.
\]

Therefore, at any conventional level such as \(\alpha=0.05\), reject \(H_0\). There is strong evidence of a seed-by-fertilizer interaction; the fertilizer effect is not the same for all seed types.

---

## (3) Test fertilizer has no effect for every seed type

This hypothesis is stronger than the ordinary fertilizer main-effect test. It says that within each seed type, the fertilizer means are equal:

\[
H_0:\ \mu_{i1}=\mu_{i2}=\mu_{i3}
\quad \text{for each seed type } i=1,2,3.
\]

Equivalently, the model under \(H_0\) contains seed effects only, with no fertilizer effect and no seed-fertilizer interaction. Thus we compare the full two-way model to the reduced seed-only model.

The numerator sum of squares is therefore

\[
SS_{\text{Fertilizer}}+SS_{\text{Seed:Fertilizer}}
=11.820+47.949=59.769.
\]

The numerator degrees of freedom are

\[
2+4=6.
\]

So the test statistic is

\[
F=\frac{(SS_{\text{Fertilizer}}+SS_{\text{Interaction}})/6}{MS_E}
=
\frac{59.769/6}{45.210/36}.
\]

Compute:

\[
\frac{59.769}{6}=9.9615,
\]

so

\[
F=\frac{9.9615}{1.25583}=7.932.
\]

Under \(H_0\),

\[
F\sim F_{6,36}.
\]

The \(p\)-value is approximately

\[
p \approx 1.7\times 10^{-5}.
\]

Thus we reject \(H_0\). There is strong evidence that fertilizer has an effect for at least one seed type. Note that because the interaction is significant, the ordinary fertilizer main-effect test alone is not the appropriate test for “no fertilizer effect for every seed type”; the correct numerator uses both the fertilizer and interaction sums of squares.
